output.name: Lavesk
output.myth: When the Gale Tavo took a boat off the skerries, the men went down under the water and did not come up. Their wives set the kettle on and waited. By morning the shags stood on the rock with their wings held out to dry, and the old women said that was the drowned, come up to spread their cloth. Mother Hesk told the wives not to look too long. A shag that is watched keeps its wings spread and never leaves the rock. Sil, who searches for her brother Aun, has seen them, and says they are only drying their sails. Kael the Netter comes down at low tide with his empty net to fish for lamps, and has never caught one. Halvun the ray, away south-west, saw the boat go first and keeps the count of who went down. Ommen, the Lamp Boat, carries a lantern for each name said at the harbour mouth. So when you see the birds at dawn, turn from them, put the kettle on, say the names of the drowned, then go in and mend your nets.
output.finding: From Ommen, the Lamp Boat, look a fist and a little more to the north-west, and the Drying Shag will be standing low over the southern sea.
